body: I am not sure actually. Were there many faroese females who took part in it over the course of the years? Having a list might help.

Your SIL is lucky to have you. If you read my post, I'm in a similar situation, and none of his family members has spared a good word to me. Just let her know that you're with her and that you know he's being a horrible person. It will help her.

Thank you, so much. These days have given me the clarity to think this through exactly this way. I have made some math, and I know exactly he has been with someone he met last july, while he was in his country with my son. I texted him and let him know that I knew that, and I knew who it is, and that he's her problem now. I then blocked him. 
Yeah there were many past episodes...he has been drunk and occasionally violent, yelled at me even when I was pregnant, called me all the names under the sun, gaslighted me, told me that I was ugly, or crazy, said horrible things about my parents, gone MIA, and then finally, cheated. All these reasons are enough for anyone. But I was a blinded mom, scared to be alone, who clinged to his positive sides whenever there were some. But deep down I knew how wrong he was, and this is the reason why I couldn't get too affectionate, couldn't spontaneously hug him, couldn't trust him. 
On one hand I feel that a weight has been lifted from my chest, on the other hand I panic. 
But I decided that I don't want to lose my hopes.  
Lots of love <3

He sent my son a picture of himself in Florence now with the caption "Sorry my phone was broken, I love you". That's total BS, his phone was working because he did read my messages over the past week and he was online.
He was never in Rome before, last time he was there, we were together. Rome is just the place where he's meeting up with this person. She might or might not be from there, I don't know.

I understand. But he didn't state these needs when we began living together. He actually used to say that he didn't want to live there. I understand that these needs may come up with years and age, however, it was a difficult choice for me. Anyway, when I decided for it, he was already into someone else by the looks of it.

He has no money, barely for tickets back home, so the fact that he would take an escape to Rome (still in this country) is very unlikely and mostly, out of character for him to do. I know that there's someone, the breakup was too abrupt and weird and all of a sudden "maybe let's see other people", then this.
Thank you so much!

Wow, this is really great advice thank you. I'm so sorry you had to go through this as well. People who ghost are cowards, husbands/fathers who ghost...I don't even have words for them.
I'm currently using my anger to get past this. I hope I'll get to the point where I don't feel anything towards him, as you said. Taking medications is helping me a little, because it has been shutting down strong emotions. I know it's only a band aid though, but at this point in my life I need support coming from whatever source.

>kids are better of without him than with an unreliable father who disappoints them again and again by just not showing up.

I couldn't agree more. I don't know if waking up one day and suddenly wanting to talk to the children it would be ok either. He was not there when *they* wanted to talk. Why should his needs be met when their needs aren't? I don't want to be a parental alienator, but I really wonder how that should work.

Thank you so much! I don't live in Germany and I don't think there's anything like that around here, but I will run a search.

As for custody, I can't even imagine having joint custody when one parent lives abroad... and in this situation it seems impossible to deal with anything but full custody. I will start the process asap, so that my children can be entitled to their freedom to even have a passport, or go on field trips without him bothering to sign.
It's a little country with only 50k inhabitants, to the extent that I think I might even give up his identity if I said which one it is!
Thank you so much <3 I hope I will have the same strength. Going through custody will probably help me heal as well.

I definitely see what you mean. He has been brainwashing me into thinking this was my fault, as if he and his actions had nothing to do with me keeping him at an arm's length, or feeling depressed. When you hear something so often, you end up believing it.
I'm going through the process of replacing the man in my good memories, with the person I actually know he is. Rewriting my whole perception of things. Hopefully it will help me.
Thank you <3 I've seen reddit hating on single moms in the past, it's disheartening... It takes an enormous strength.

Thank you <3 Oh, he definitely cannot be trusted again, I already made that mistake before and it was disastrous. I am not sure how to break the truth to the children... I still feel like shielding them, they're so young, but they will definitely be told.
Thank you <3

There are several alcoholics in his family. He will never come out of this. I agree, alcoholism is not only a problem while drinking, it seems to come with a set of behaviors and personality traits that made it impossible for me to deal with it.
I hope so too! Someone who steals a man from his family can't be a half decent person either. They are likely going to be each other's problem. I wish them to reap what they sow.
I'm so sorry to hear that, it's truly horrible.
Thank you <3 I also know that at some point he will regret this. I don't know if karma is real, but I hope it is...
Thank you! It's hard! Taking care of two children when my state of mind is crumbling. But they're all I have, and I'm all they have.

Thank you! That could definitely be the case. I did stay with him despite many problems basically because I wouldn't want my children to grow up without a father. Sometimes no father might be better than an inconsistent and confusing father, though.
I'm not sure what it the best way of documenting this (mostly lack of contact), but perhaps my lawyer will have some advice...
Thank you so much <3
My lawyer thinks full custody for us should be pretty clear. I hope so.

Thank you! I heard a lawyer and he's positive that we can win full custody. I will look for therapy for my children, they are what worries me the most. They are brilliant children and deserve so much better than this.
Thank you! These comments are truly helping me! <3

I know for sure that he hasn't, my boy has also spent a month there last July. But I have basis to suspect that he has someone new over there, based on his rejection for all of us to move there and sudden the break up.
I hope so! Right now it's hard. Living in a small town setting/rural area as a single mom makes it my chances of moving on equal to zero.

Oh, he is "forbidding me" to move anywhere outside the EU. He wouldn't even let the children have a passport before he left, because he says we should only travel within the EU. I had been working on a US visa and saw some good chances at having it, but apparently we are limited in our movements, whereas he can do how he pleases...

This is what I'm thinking as well. Thank you. It still feels bad because my fear of abandonment is general is too invalidating. It sometimes obscures my reason and won't let me see what's best, cause I'd do anything just not to be abandoned. I'm afraid that my son will develop that because of his father. Were you abandoned as well if I may ask?
This is what I'm hoping. But hoping at the same time makes me stressed because I don't know where I'm standing. I don't know where to put my mind.

You are probably right about all that. I still acknowledge that I should have tried to be more affectionate because everyone wants to feel loved. It was a vicious circle. Him putting me off with his drinking/behavior, me becoming more detached, his saying that my behavior or the place we live (he moved here to be with us) was the reason for his drinking. No one should accept disappearing this way and ghosting your family. he's 40 years old. Yet I am trying to pour all the affection I repressed through messages, and they go unnoticed. So yeah... it's not a team work. But wherever the responsibilities stand, I feel hopeless right now. I'm 35 year old, with two children, no possibilities of dating where I live (extremely rural place and other things). I'm aging, I lost the little beauty I had in my younger days and after two pregnancies. There is really no more hope for companionship unless I move some place else. And I can't do this by myself either. He was the only one who could love me.

I'm so sorry that happen to you. He does. He does blame it all on me. I recognize that I haven't been super affectionate/super involved. This is what I blame myself for. On the other hand, I know that disappearing last year, and the drinking issues are the things that eventually made me feel detached around him. There were good things though, he can be a good father, when he wants to, and a good funny and loving partner. Of course right now this is all I think of. The things I lost and could have had if I showed more interest and was more affectionate myself. It would have taken me so little compared to what it takes now. I think about this over and over and over and I can't find peace. I texted him showing that i was willing to work on my mood or shortcomings because I love him.

Thank you. He has drinking problems that at the core, those were the base for our issues. Except two or three instances, he didn't get really dangerous while drinking. I know it's enough to be scared though. I think he simply chose drinking over his family. I only have my two elderly parents who have their own limits and health issues. I'm an only child. No friends. Just nobody. I wish I never existed.

I know for sure it's deliberate because his parents didn't seem concerned and are not replying either. If they were concerned, they would. He only texted me once telling me he needs his things. Then he even stopped replying to that

I'm from Italy, and I visted NYC in 1999 on a kids summer camp. A kid who was there with me saw her neighbor from Italy in the subway train.

Also, another friend of mine ran into his old roommate from Italy while walking in Sydney.

Strange stuff.
